01 / ABOUT ME

More than a name.

INFORMATIVE · THE FACTS
HELLO, I’M AURORA

I connect language with the way people see the world.

My academic background is in English and Applied Linguistics, with a minor in Hotel Management at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. My experience spans English teaching, project administration and exhibition support.

I’m interested in how language and culture shape meaning, from classroom interaction to the stories told in a music video.

04 / SELECTED WORK

Where my curiosity gets loud.

EXPRESSIVE · MY PERSPECTIVE
FEATURED · UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH · 2025

Beyond the beat.

Multimodal Metaphor in Narrative Perspective: The Influence of K-pop Music Videos on Fan Identity

✳

For me, a music video is a text worth reading closely. In this project, I explored how lyrics, visual design and choreography build stories of identity, resistance and belonging.

Two MVs. Two ways of claiming a place in the world.
STRENGTH
IN UNITY
SEVENTEEN / SUPER

Myth. Movement. Collective strength.

I read the MV through the metaphor “Life is War”: Sun Wukong imagery, martial movement and synchronised formations become a story of discipline and collective resistance.

MYTHOLOGYCHOREOGRAPHYIDENTITY
IDENTITY
ON MY TERMS
I-DLE / TOMBOY

The self, reclaimed.

I interpret “Identity is Rebellion” through dollhouse imagery and gestures of refusal. The contrast between confinement and freedom offers a way to read resistance to imposed gender roles.

RESEARCH / READING NOTES

How I approached it

A qualitative analysis combining conceptual metaphor theory, multimodal discourse analysis and narrative analysis. I examined how lyrics, visual design and gestures work together.

What the study can—and cannot—show

These are interpretations of two music videos. They suggest how identity can be represented in the texts; they do not establish a measured causal effect on fans. The study also leaves sonic metaphor for future research.
